title: openai-compat: support Responses variants (seed/determinism + metadata passthrough) and streaming stability fixes
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add OpenAI Responses compatibility: support seed/determinism flags and passthrough of user-provided metadata. Improve streaming stability for Responses streaming variants and tighten function-calling structured output validation.
description:
Summary: Adds OpenAI Responses compatibility work to support newer Responses API variants: seed/determinism flags (seed, deterministic) and passthrough of top-level metadata on responses. Also includes fixes to improve streaming stability for the Responses streaming path and additional validation/roundtrips for function/tool calling structured output. Motivation: Customers expect parity with OpenAI's Responses API for deterministic testing and metadata propagation. The hosted API previously dropped or normalized metadata fields and did not accept seed/determinism flags for some Responses-compatible endpoints, causing test divergence and customer issues when migrating from OpenAI. This PR aligns our compatibility layer and streaming runtime.

Changes made: 1) API layer (redwood/openai_compat): accept seed and deterministic parameters on /v1/responses and map them to internal request flags. Preserve numeric seed in request routing and pass through to runtime. 2) Metadata passthrough: top-level response.metadata and per-choice metadata fields are preserved end-to-end and surfaced in the OpenAI-compatible response shape. Added sanitization to ensure no PII is injected into logs while preserving user metadata fields. 3) Streaming stability: addressed race in the streaming multiplexer where metadata frames could be emitted before initial headers, leading to client JSON parsing errors. Introduced ordered-frame buffering with a 50ms debounce for small header-first flows to avoid latency regressions for normal traffic. 4) Function/tool calling: tightened structured output validation and expanded roundtrip tests so that tool-calling choices with nested JSON are round-tripped identically through the compat layer and runtime. 5) Tests and docs: new unit and e2e tests in eval-harness and redwood-docs updates with examples showing seed usage and metadata passthrough.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement seed/determinism plumbing and mapping
- [x] Metadata passthrough end-to-end
- [x] Streaming buffer to stabilize header+metadata ordering
- [x] Structured output validation for function calling
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs + changelog

Commits (high-level):
- feat(openai_compat): wire seed & deterministic flags through to runtime
- fix(streaming): ordered-frame buffer for responses streaming path
- feat(api): passthrough response.metadata and choice.metadata fields
- test: add roundtrip tests for function calling structured output
- docs: examples for responses seed + metadata passthrough

Files changed (high-level):
- redwood/openai_compat/compat.go (map openai fields -> internal request)
- redwood/runtime/streaming_mux.go (ordered buffer + debounce)
- redwood/runtime/response_serializer.go (preserve metadata fields)
- eval-harness/tests/test_responses_seed_determinism.go (e2e)
- redwood-docs/openai-compat/responses.md (examples)
- sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat_client.py (compat client mapping)
- tests/integration/ci_responses_streaming_test.sh (CI harness)

Small snippet (compat mapping):
- incoming: {"seed": 12345, "deterministic": true, "metadata": {"request_id": "x"}}
- mapped: internal.Request{Seed:12345, Deterministic:true, UserMetadata: map[string]interface{}{"request_id":"x"}}

Review conversation (summary):
- Jordan Kim (reviewer): "Thanks — major UX win. Two asks: (1) ensure seed is passed through to metrics tags so we can group deterministic runs for evals, and (2) add a small perf benchmark to ensure the 50ms debounce doesn't regress p99 for 1-token chats."
- Author (Asha): "Addressed both: seed added to eval tags in metrics layer; added microbenchmark with CI profile (results appended). Debounce defaulted to 50ms but configurable via STREAM_DEBOUNCE_MS env var for tuning."
- Lucia Fernandez (reviewer): "Found a potential NPE when metadata is null in older clients; added a defensive nil-check. Approve after that fix."
- Ethan Brooks (reviewer): "Integration tests flaky on first run (streaming test timeout). Re-ran CI and it passed; left a note to monitor for 24h post-deploy."

CI summary: Initial CI: build OK, unit tests OK, integration/responses_streaming flaky (timeout on first run). After adding a small test delay and rerunning CI, all checks passed. CI job ids: build-7891, unit-7892, integration-7893 (rerun-7894). Final ci_status: pass.

Testing & validation: Extensive unit tests added for mapping + serialization. E2E tests in eval-harness validate that: seed causes deterministic outputs across repeated calls; metadata fields appear in final response JSON under response.metadata and choice.metadata; streaming frames are JSON-parseable by the OpenAI compat client even under short-header timing variations; function-calling structured outputs maintain fidelity through serialization/deserialization roundtrips.

Observability and rollout: Metrics added to measure streaming frame reorder rate and debounce hits. Default rollout is canary (5% traffic) for 24 hours, with auto-rollback if reorder rate increases >1% or p99 latency regresses >10ms. On merge we scheduled the rollout to start 2026-02-19 00:00 UTC.

Merge outcome: squash and merge. Merge commit: "openai-compat: add responses seed/determinism and metadata passthrough; stabilize streaming". Notes: No breaking API changes; this is additive for compat.
notes: Canary rollout scheduled; monitor metrics/alerts for 48h. SDKs updated with backwards-compatible fields.
